clue.text: A bachelor meeting Elizabeth, a superior woman

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
Bess is a pet form of the name Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A single man is introduced to a woman called Elizabeth who carries herself as rather grand.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as snobbery, but a superior here is the head of a religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess is the female head of a convent, a Mother Superior over its nuns.

clue.text: The aisle, do we hear, where horses may be ridden?

indicators.note: asking whether we hear it signals a word spoken like the meaning, though spelt otherwise

blocks.note: the aisle is the route a bride walks at a wedding

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a church aisle is fit for riding horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridleway is a British public path on which horse riders, as well as walkers, have right of way.

clue.text: Be slow about forcing one's way through with these?

definitions.text: forcing one's way through with these?

indicators.note: about can mean round and round in no fixed order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice not to rush when pushing through a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as concerning, but here it shuffles the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: People shove through crowds by jabbing with the joints of their arms, hence to elbow one's way through.

clue.text: The old SS had power to move you

definitions.text: The old SS had power to move you

blocks.clueFragment: The old SS had power to move you
blocks.note: surface reading: something emotionally stirring about an old organisation or an initialism
setter's reading: a vessel of old, whose name prefix is SS, was driven by steam to carry passengers

explanation.surface: A remark that the old SS could stir the emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: SS before a ship's name stands for the vessel type; 'move you' sounds emotional but means transport you across the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships with SS before their names were powered by steam engines and carried passengers in the age before diesel.

clue.text: Warders' wages small

definitions.note: read as 'warders are', a plural noun

blocks.note: screw is old British slang for a wage or salary
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A complaint that prison officers are poorly paid.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe makes 'Warders' look possessive, but it stands for 'Warders is', the definition followed by the wordplay. Screws is British prison slang for warders.
explanation.definitionFit: In British prison slang the guards are called screws, from the turnkeys who locked cells.

clue.text: So many taking part in athletics event

indicators.note: taking part in means being contained within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and into the second

explanation.surface: A count of competitors entered in a track-and-field contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So many' is a deliberately vague stand-in for a number, which the clue words then specify.
explanation.definitionFit: A number can be defined as 'so many', meaning a specific quantity of things.

clue.text: Foul-smelling fish causing irritation

blocks.note: rank means having a strong, unpleasant smell
the ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: A smelly fish is annoying someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles keeps annoying or embittering a person long after the event.

clue.text: Keep shaking the cart

blocks.note: a dog's tail wags when it is shaken to and fro
to keep doing something is to carry on with it

explanation.surface: An order to go on jolting a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'wag on' is to keep wagging, so the two clue words are read in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a four-wheeled vehicle for carrying loads, much like a cart.

clue.text: One slides over nail to avoid a puncture

definitions.text: One slides over nail to avoid a puncture

blocks.clueFragment: One slides over nail to avoid a puncture
blocks.note: surface reading: something like a tyre guard or a carpenter's device sliding over a metal nail
setter's reading: the nail is a fingernail, and the puncture comes from a sewing needle

explanation.surface: Some device fits over a nail so a tyre or foot does not get pierced.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress wears a small metal cap over the fingertip so the needle does not prick the finger.

clue.text: A listed building?

blocks.note: surface reading: a building protected by heritage listing for its historic value
setter's reading: listing as a ship does, tilting to one side

explanation.surface: A question about whether some structure has protected heritage status.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a listed building is one legally protected for its history; to list also means to lean over.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Italian bell tower leans several degrees off vertical, so it literally lists.

clue.text: Condiment given a false rating at first

indicators.note: something false is not genuine, so the letters are set out in a counterfeit order
at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the opening letter of rating

explanation.surface: A sauce or relish has been awarded an undeserved score at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar is a sour liquid used to season or preserve food, a standard table condiment.

clue.text: Wrongly record event — it's changed back

indicators.note: something done wrongly is done amiss, so these letters come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mistake in the records has been put right again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvert is to convert again, returning something to its earlier form or faith.

clue.text: Health centre for hypochondriacs?

blocks.note: straight reading: a clinic offering routine health checks for women
setter's reading: a place for people who are in fact well but think they are ill

explanation.surface: A joke about a medical clinic catering to people who imagine they are sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The name of a real kind of clinic is read literally as a place where healthy women go for treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: These British clinics give routine screening and advice to women who are not ill, which suits worriers about their health.

clue.text: Arguments got louder, as we hear

indicators.note: as we hear asks for a word that is spoken like the one meant, not spelt like it

blocks.note: a voice that got louder rose in volume

explanation.surface: Quarrels became noisier, as the neighbours could tell.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the plural noun for quarrels, rhyming with cows, but the clue relies on the other pronunciation that rhymes with nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows is a British word for noisy quarrels or disputes.

clue.text: Two terms of golf that go with your card

blocks.note: first meaning: a chip is a short lofted shot and the pin is the flagstick, joined by and
second meaning: the British name for paying by bank card and typing a personal number

explanation.surface: Golf jargon that a player writes on a scorecard.
explanation.walkthrough: The card looks like a golf scorecard, but it is a bank card used in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The payment system pairs a microchip in the card with a personal identification number keyed in at the till.

clue.text: Drunk port, No 1 in wine

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so these letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Port, after drinking, ranked as the best wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 1' looks like a ranking, but it is split into the word no and the numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot noir is a black grape variety and the red wine made from it, famous in Burgundy.

clue.text: No amateur was keen to be dragged out

blocks.note: someone who is not an amateur is a professional
to have longed for something is to have been keen on it

explanation.surface: A professional eager to have a contest drawn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prolonged has been extended in time, lasting longer than needed.

clue.text: Paper, large amount, for an appointment

blocks.note: The Times is the London daily newspaper
a lot is a large amount

explanation.surface: Plenty of paper is needed for a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A time slot is an allotted period in a schedule, the kind booked for an appointment.

clue.text: Unauthorised disposal of insect?

blocks.note: straight reading: illegal dumping of rubbish
setter's reading: the tipping out of a small flying bug

explanation.surface: Someone illegally gets rid of a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The everyday British term for illegal rubbish dumping is read literally, as if the thing tipped were an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain, dumping waste on land without permission is called by this name, a criminal offence.

clue.text: Manage to get last member of oil cartel into leading position

indicators.note: picks out the final letter of the following word as the one to be moved
sending that final letter to the front rotates the word one place round

blocks.note: the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries is the oil producers' cartel

explanation.surface: Instructions for handling a takeover so the newest oil-cartel member ends up in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to deal successfully with a difficulty, to get by or manage.

clue.text: Fields of study concerned with charitable giving

blocks.note: re means regarding or about
alms are gifts of money or food to the poor

explanation.surface: Academic subjects dealing with philanthropy.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or sphere of activity, so realms of knowledge are fields of study.

clue.text: Coming to the end of touring holiday with no alternative available?

definitions.text: Coming to the end of touring holiday

blocks.clueFragment: Coming to the end of touring holiday
blocks.note: first meaning, literal: at the final stopping place of a tour
second meaning, idiom: as a final option when all else has failed

explanation.surface: A traveller reaches the final stop of a tour with nowhere else to go.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means when every other option has been tried, so only this course remains.

clue.text: Slight colour in metal regularly grey

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: tin is a common metal
the first and third letters of grey

explanation.surface: A faint hue showing in a dull grey metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a trace or faint shade of a colour.

clue.text: Extra notice given to teacher

blocks.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A teacher is handed an additional warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is an additional item or feature supplied with something else.

clue.text: Line and wriggly worm

indicators.note: something wriggly squirms about, so the letters twist into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a worm as a thin wiggling line.
explanation.definitionFit: Annelids are the segmented worms, a zoological group that includes earthworms and leeches.

clue.text: Under compulsion, old boy told a story about golf

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for telling a story wraps round the next letter

blocks.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
telling a story is a polite way to say telling a fib
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A former pupil, pressed into it, spun a yarn about a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Being obliged to do something means being bound or forced to do it.

clue.text: Gravedigger working after an hour in church

blocks.note: Sext is the canonical office said at the sixth hour, around noon
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A gravedigger puts in a shift after spending an hour at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the second piece behind the first; the church hour is one of the monastic daily offices.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church caretaker whose traditional duties include digging graves and ringing bells.

clue.text: Furious desire to live

indicators.note: something furious is wild and frenzied, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A passionate urge to stay alive.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to dwell or have one's home there, to live in a place.
